To improve upon this by capturing more signal and reducing variance from the dominant trend, I will test a robust combination over a slightly larger pool of the best performers (pool5), specifically using DBA which is designed to handle diverse model outputs.

The current leader (mean on THETA+ETS) is very strong and hard to beat. Since ranking is unstable and we have a trend-dominated series, I will test a robust combination using DBA on the top-performing subset (pool4: THETA, ETS) to see if it can stabilize the forecast better than simple mean/trimmed_mean.

The current leader (a7) relies on a simple mean of the two top models (THETA, ETS). To test if weighting by inverse error improves upon this equal-weight baseline for this specific pair, I will evaluate the weighted combination using inverse_error weights on pool4. This tests the hypothesis that THETA and ETS have sufficiently different error profiles to warrant unequal weighting, despite their high correlation.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9548. Series context: trend strength 0.9888 and seasonal strength 0.5278; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.053); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.954.
